summary: 从被掠卖为奴的羯人少年到开国称帝，都襄国、灭前赵而臣北方，十六国最具戏剧性的创业者。
summary_en: A Jie youth kidnapped and sold into slavery who rose to found an empire — ruling from Xiangguo, he destroyed Former Zhao and made the north submit, the most dramatic state-founder of the Sixteen Kingdoms.

bio_md:
# 后赵高祖 · 主要事迹

石勒是羯人，少时约当西晋永兴前后被掠卖为奴，后来聚众起兵，最终登上帝位——从奴隶到天子的跨度，使他成为十六国史里最戏剧性的创业者。本页以《晋书》卷一百四至一百五石勒载记为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴》编年。

创业之初，他一度归入刘渊、刘聪的汉赵系统，借汉赵旗帜在华北作战中积累实力。永嘉五年（311）洛阳陷落前后，他参与永嘉之乱后的华北混战，军势迅速坐大，成为割据一方的主力。

太兴二年（319），石勒称赵王、都襄国，正式脱离前赵阴影，后赵政权由此成立；两年后进称大单于，名号与制度同步升格。咸和三年至四年（328–329），他与前赵末主刘曜在洛阳一线决战，破刘曜、灭前赵，北方大部归入后赵版图。咸和五年（330），他在襄国称皇帝，帝制完备，完成了从奴隶到天子的全过程。

石勒并非只有武功。他以张宾为谋主，兴学校、定制度，设君子营安置士人，在胡汉分治的框架下做秩序建设的探索。需要注意，史籍中后赵的残暴记载多须区分石勒本人与其后继者石虎；对石勒本人，史家仍称其雄略。

咸和八年（333），石勒崩于襄国。他生前安排的继承人石弘旋即为石虎所夺，后赵政治迅速恶化，国祚不长。与[[q-qin-fu-jian|前秦苻坚]]对读：同为十六国胡人政权的立国或中兴之主，一前一后，可见那个时代创业与治乱的不同路径。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Le was a Jie. In his youth, around the Yongxing era of the Western Jin, he was kidnapped and sold into slavery; he later gathered a following, rose in arms, and finally ascended the imperial throne — the span from slave to Son of Heaven makes him the most dramatic state-founder in the history of the Sixteen Kingdoms. This page takes the Shi Le annals in juan 104–105 of the 《晋书》 as its chronological backbone, supplemented by the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴》.

At the start of his enterprise he attached himself for a time to the Han-Zhao system of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong, building strength through campaigns in north China under the Han-Zhao banner. Around the fall of Luoyang in Yongjia 5 (311), he joined the melee that followed the Yongjia upheaval in north China; his military power swelled rapidly, making him a leading force among the regional powers.

In Taixing 2 (319) Shi Le took the title King of Zhao and made Xiangguo his capital, formally stepping out of Former Zhao's shadow — the Later Zhao regime was thereby founded; two years later he advanced to Great Chanyu, his titles and institutions rising in step. In Xianhe 3–4 (328–329) he fought the decisive battle along the Luoyang line against Liu Yao, the last ruler of Former Zhao: he defeated Liu Yao, destroyed Former Zhao, and most of the north entered the Later Zhao map. In Xianhe 5 (330) he proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo, completing the imperial system — and with it the entire passage from slave to Son of Heaven.

Shi Le was not a man of martial feats alone. He made Zhang Bin his chief strategist, promoted schools and fixed institutions, established the Gentlemen's Camp to house men of letters, and explored the building of order within the framework of Hu-Han dual rule. One caveat: the records of Later Zhao cruelty in the histories must often be divided between Shi Le himself and his successor Shi Hu; of Shi Le himself, historians still speak of his boldness of design.

In Xianhe 8 (333) Shi Le died at Xiangguo. Shi Hong, the heir he had arranged, was at once dispossessed by Shi Hu; Later Zhao politics deteriorated quickly, and the dynastic line did not last long. Read him against
: both were founders or restorers of Hu states in the Sixteen Kingdoms period, one earlier and one later, and together they show the era's different paths of state-building and of order and collapse.
